root_cause.text: The kernel's resume path for the local APIC (lapic_resume) did not verify or revert the x2apic hardware state if firmware re-enabled it during S2/S3 resume, causing a mismatch where the kernel continued using the xapic interface while the hardware operated in x2apic mode, leading to hangs.
root_cause.evidence: The commit description explicitly states: "When resuming from s2ram, firmware may re-enable x2apic mode... This causes the kernel to continue using the xapic interface, while the hardware is in x2apic mode, which causes hangs." The fix adds a check in lapic_resume() to call __x2apic_disable() when the kernel expects x2apic disabled (x2apic_mode == 0) but the hardware has it enabled (x2apic_enabled() returns true).

intent_record.intent_summary: Add stub for __x2apic_disable when x2apic is disabled to avoid undefined function errors.
intent_record.what: Added a static inline stub function __x2apic_disable(void) inside the #ifndef CONFIG_X86_X2APIC block, providing an empty implementation.
intent_record.how: This makes __x2apic_disable available as a no-op when CONFIG_X86_X2APIC is disabled, preventing compilation errors if code calls this function without x2apic support.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard in lapic_resume to disable x2APIC if firmware re-enables it during resume when kernel expects xAPIC mode.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check and call to __x2apic_disable() inside the else branch (when x2apic_mode is false) in lapic_resume, if x2apic_enabled() returns true.
intent_record.how: During resume, if the system is not in x2apic mode but the firmware has re-enabled x2APIC, the kernel will disable it, ensuring the expected xAPIC mode.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 659006bf3ae37a08706907ce1a36ddf57c9131d2
Author: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@kernel.org>
Date:   Thu Jan 15 21:22:26 2015 +0000

    x86/x2apic: Split enable and setup function
    
    enable_x2apic() is a convoluted unreadable mess because it is used for
    both enablement in early boot and for setup in cpu_init().
    
    Split the code into x2apic_enable() for enablement and x2apic_setup()
    for setup of (secondary cpus). Make use of the new state tracking to
    simplify the logic.
bic_trace_step.reason: In lapic_resume, after this commit, if x2apic_mode is true, __x2apic_enable() is called, but if x2apic_mode is false, the else block does nothing to disable x2apic in case firmware re-enabled it during resume. This leaves the vulnerable mismatch where kernel uses xapic interface while hardware is in x2apic mode, matching the root cause. No fix (verification or reverting) is added.
